# The Mass Spectrum {#sec-masses}

All particle masses in FTD are derived from three quantities: the Planck mass $m_P$ (the only dimensionful input), the fine structure constant $\alpha$ (from the master quadratic), and the framework integers $\{3, 4, 7, 13\}$ (from the lattice geometry). This chapter presents the mass formulas and their accuracy.

## The electron mass [SELECTION]

$$
m_e = m_P \sqrt{2\pi} \cdot \frac{N_{\text{base}}^2}{N_c} \cdot \alpha^{11} = m_P \sqrt{2\pi} \cdot \frac{16}{3} \cdot \alpha^{11}
\tag{12.1}
$$

Numerically: $m_e = 0.5124$ MeV (experimental: $0.5110$ MeV, error: 0.27%).

The structure: $m_P$ sets the scale. $\sqrt{2\pi}$ is the Gaussian phase-space factor. $16/3 = N_{\text{base}}^2/N_c$ is the ratio of DOF to colors. The power $\alpha^{11}$ arises from the 11th step of the alpha ladder (below).

**Epistemic status:** The formula is [SELECTION]. The power $\alpha^{11}$ and the prefactor $\sqrt{2\pi} \cdot 16/3$ are identified from the pattern, not derived from a first-principles mass generation mechanism. What would upgrade to [THEOREM]: a derivation of the electron self-energy from the lattice Lagrangian yielding this exact formula.

## The alpha power ladder [SELECTION]

Each fundamental mass scale is $m_P$ times a prefactor times a power of $\alpha$:

| $n$ | Scale | Formula | Value | Experimental |
|-----|-------|---------|-------|-------------|
| 0 | Planck mass | $m_P$ | $1.221 \times 10^{19}$ GeV | Definition |
| 2 | GUT scale | $m_P \cdot \alpha^2$ | $\sim 2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV | $\sim 2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV |
| 8 | Electroweak VEV | $m_P \sqrt{2\pi} \cdot \alpha^8$ | 246.08 GeV | 246.22 GeV (0.06%) |
| 11 | Electron mass | $m_P \sqrt{2\pi} \cdot (16/3) \cdot \alpha^{11}$ | 0.5124 MeV | 0.5110 MeV (0.27%) |
| 20 | Gravitational coupling | $\alpha_G = \alpha^{20} \cdot \text{prefactor}$ | $1.75 \times 10^{-45}$ | $\sim 10^{-45}$ |

The ladder has integer-spaced rungs in powers of $\alpha$, with gaps $\{2, 6, 3, 9\}$ that relate to the framework integers. [SELECTION for the ladder structure]

## The proton mass [SELECTION]

$$
\frac{m_p}{m_e} = \frac{N_{\text{eff}}}{\alpha} + N_{\text{base}} \cdot N_{\text{eff}} + N_c = \frac{13}{1/137.036} + 4 \times 13 + 3
\tag{12.2}
$$

$$
= 1781.47 + 52 + 3 = 1836.47
$$

Experimental: $m_p/m_e = 1836.15267$ (error: 174 ppm = 0.017%).

The three terms have physical interpretations:
- $N_{\text{eff}}/\alpha$: the valence quark contribution (13 effective DOF at coupling $\alpha$)
- $N_{\text{base}} \cdot N_{\text{eff}}$: the sea quark and gluon contribution (52 modes)
- $N_c$: the color binding energy correction (3 confined colors)

[SELECTION --- the decomposition into three terms is identified from the pattern]

## The Higgs mass [SELECTION]

The Higgs VEV:
$$
v = m_P \sqrt{2\pi} \cdot \alpha^8 = 246.08 \text{ GeV} \quad (\text{exp: } 246.22 \text{ GeV, 0.06\%})
\tag{12.3}
$$

The Higgs quartic coupling:
$$
\lambda_H = \frac{\sin^2\theta_W}{2 - \sin^2\theta_W} = \frac{3/13}{2 - 3/13} = \frac{3}{23}
\tag{12.4}
$$

The Higgs mass (two formulas, both [SELECTION]):
$$
m_H = v\sqrt{\frac{6}{23}} = 125.69 \text{ GeV} \quad (\text{exp: } 125.25 \text{ GeV, 0.35\%})
\tag{12.5}
$$

An alternative formula gives $m_H = (N_{\text{eff}}/\alpha^2) \cdot m_e = 124.8$ GeV (0.40% error). The two formulas differ by $\sim 1$ GeV, reflecting different routes through the framework integers. The Weinberg angle $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/13 = N_c/N_{\text{eff}}$ is [SELECTION]. The Higgs quartic $\lambda_H = 3/23$ follows algebraically from $\sin^2\theta_W$ via the ternary decomposition. [SELECTION for the physical identifications]

## The lepton mass ratios [SELECTION]

$$
\frac{m_\mu}{m_e} \approx 207 = N_c \cdot b_3 \cdot (b_3 + N_c) - N_c = 3 \times 7 \times 10 - 3
$$

$$
\frac{m_\tau}{m_e} \approx 3477 = 3 \times 19 \times 61
$$

These ratios involve the framework integers but the exact formulas are less clean than for the electron or proton. The muon and tau masses are [SELECTION] with $\sim 1\%$ accuracy. [OPEN for a clean derivation]
